records.name: Pennsylvania Center for Adapted Sports (PCAS)
records.summary: A nonprofit on Boathouse Row that runs sports and wellness programs for people with disabilities, for adults and for young athletes. Members can row, climb, kayak, ski, or take part in yoga and pickleball.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a sport, join a session with coaches and volunteers, or volunteer to help run programs and events.

schedule.text: Programs run through the year, and rowing runs May to October. Dates and times vary by sport, so check the program pages.

cost.text: Program fees are not listed on the pages we checked.

access.notes: The site describes its settings as barrier free and shows hand cycling, but it has no separate wheelchair statement and no ASL statement.

first_step.how: Call the office at 215-765-5118 or use the contact form to ask which sport fits you
first_step.basis: Open to the public with listed programs, a contact form, and a volunteer page, but the site does not describe a beginner day.

records.notes: Umbrella for Philadelphia Adaptive Rowing, which has its own record. A climbing listing on adaptiverechub.org points here. That listing has no dates and shows a phone number belonging to that platform, which was not used. The site has no dated news, so status is probably_active, not active. Program counts differ between pages (12 or 13).

records.name: Philadelphia Adaptive Rowing (PAR)
records.summary: Rowing for people with disabilities on the Schuylkill River, run by the Pennsylvania Center for Adapted Sports. Members can row for fun or race, with coaches who have college and national team experience.
records.what_you_do: Row on the river from May through October with coaches and volunteers. Equipment is provided, and some rowers go on to regattas.

schedule.text: May through October, Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 5:30 pm until dusk, per the PCAS rowing page. An older listing says Monday to Wednesday, so confirm before going.

cost.text: No fee is listed for rowers. Equipment is provided.

access.notes: Equipment and coaches are provided at each session. The page does not say how wheelchair users take part or whether ASL is offered, so ask first.

first_step.how: Fill in the rower form on the PCAS rowing page, or use the PCAS contact form
first_step.basis: Open to people 14 and up through a listed form, and the program offers recreational rowing as well as racing.

records.notes: The PCAS rowing page names a West River Drive boathouse in its text but 1233 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive in its schedule and contact page, so the record uses the Martin Luther King address. Phone is the PCAS main line, since the rowing page lists none. Founding year differs by source, so it is not recorded.

records.name: Achilles International Philadelphia
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of Achilles International, which helps people with disabilities walk, run, and race. Members set goals such as a first mile and train with volunteer guide runners.
records.what_you_do: Come to the Saturday morning session at the fitness center, work toward a goal, and join group walks or rides. Volunteers can sign up as guide runners.

schedule.text: Saturdays at 9:00 am, per the chapter page.

locations.label: Cigna Fitness Center, fourth floor, Liberty Place

cost.text: The chapter page does not say whether there is a fee.

access.notes: The chapter welcomes people who are blind or have low vision, deaf or hard of hearing, or have other disabilities, including spinal cord injuries. The page does not describe wheelchair access or ASL interpreting.

first_step.how: Use the Join button on the chapter page to register as an athlete, or contact the chapter about becoming a guide runner
first_step.basis: Open to people with disabilities with a clear registration step, though the page does not describe a beginner day.

records.notes: The email and phone are the national office's, shown on the chapter page. The chapter's own contact person is not published. Join and Volunteer buttons go to a registration login. The chapter page lists no dated items, so status is probably_active.

records.name: Special Olympics Pennsylvania, Greater Philadelphia Region
records.summary: The Pennsylvania Special Olympics program covers Philadelphia and four nearby counties. It runs year-round sports for athletes with intellectual disabilities, plus free health screenings through its Healthy Athletes program.
records.what_you_do: Train and compete as an athlete, or volunteer in one of many roles, from coaching to event help. Unified partners play on teams alongside athletes.

schedule.text: Sports and training run on schedules that vary by sport and location. The state site has a sport finder for nearby options.

locations.label: Greater Philadelphia Region office, Norristown
locations.address: 2570 Boulevard of the Generals, Suite 124, Norristown, PA 19403

cost.text: Athletic training and competitions are at no cost to athletes, per the state site.

first_step.how: Read the athlete requirements, find a sport near you, or send a message through the contact page. The state team says it replies within two business days.
first_step.basis: Open to athletes from age 2 and to volunteers, with a monthly volunteer info call or webinar, though the site does not describe a beginner day.

records.notes: Statewide organization. Its Greater Philadelphia Region covers Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia counties. The pages checked name no Philadelphia venues or sports, so a follow-up could add a city sports list. The dated item (Oct 6, 2026) is a statewide thank-you post.

records.name: The Arc of Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that speaks up for children and adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities and their families. It runs parent trainings, Zoom drop-in hours for school planning help, and a youth leadership program.
records.what_you_do: Go to a parent training or a drop-in hour for help with school planning, or ask about the youth leadership program. Families can also get referrals to other services.

schedule.text: Parent IEP training sessions and Zoom Ask the Advocate hours. Dates are posted on the site and change. Two information sessions were cancelled in 2026.

cost.text: Fees for trainings are not listed on the pages we checked.

access.notes: The site has no ASL or wheelchair statement. Ask the office about accommodations.

first_step.how: Call 215-229-4550 or send an intake form from the site, or join a Zoom Ask the Advocate hour
first_step.basis: Drop-in hours and services are open to families and individuals, with a listed phone line and intake form, though the site does not describe a welcome for newcomers.

records.notes: Part of the SpArc Philadelphia family of organizations, per its site. The newest dated item is a notice posted Oct 5, 2026 that an information session was cancelled. The youth leadership program's age range and eligibility are not on the page.

records.name: Speaking For Ourselves
records.summary: A grassroots self-advocacy group led by people with developmental disabilities. It meets online each month to build leadership skills and run its own work, with Vision for Equality as a host partner.
records.what_you_do: Join a monthly virtual meeting to talk about issues that matter to members, practice leading, and help run the group's work.

schedule.text: Monthly virtual meetings. The dates and times are not on the pages we checked.

access.notes: Meetings are online. The pages checked do not describe captioning, ASL, or other accommodations.

first_step.how: Email the group's general address to ask about the next meeting and how to join
first_step.basis: A general email is published, but the listing does not say how to join or give meeting dates, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The only source read is a Pennsylvania autism organization's listing, which files the group under support groups. The group describes itself as self-help and self-advocacy, so it is not marked as a support group. The group's own website returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The email comes from that listing and should be checked. Vision for Equality is the host partner. No dated items were found, so status is unknown.

records.name: Hearing Loss Association of America, Philadelphia Suburban/Northeast Chapter
records.summary: A chapter of the national hearing loss association for people with hearing loss and their families. It covers Bucks, Montgomery, and Philadelphia counties and meets monthly in Huntingdon Valley.
records.what_you_do: Attend the monthly evening meeting on the first Monday. Call the chapter number to confirm the date before you go.

schedule.text: Monthly on the first Monday, 6:30 to 8:30 pm, with no meetings in January, February, July, or August.

locations.label: Huntingdon Valley Library
locations.address: 625 Red Lion Road, Huntingdon Valley, PA 19006

access.notes: The listing names no accessibility features. Ask about captioning, a hearing loop, or wheelchair access before going.

first_step.how: Call the chapter number to confirm the next meeting date before you go
first_step.basis: The chapter is open to the public with a listed phone number, though the listing does not describe a welcome for newcomers.

records.notes: The only listing found is a Pennsylvania 211 directory entry, which says to call first. The state office chapter list at hlaa-pa.org does not show this chapter, and no chapter website was found, so the conflict is unresolved. Status is unknown until a dated meeting notice or post is found. The state office's Walk4Hearing at Navy Yard (Oct 18, 2026) is a one-time event and is not recorded here.

records.name: Deaf-Hearing Communication Centre (DHCC)
records.summary: A nonprofit that works for communication access for Deaf, DeafBlind, and hard of hearing people in the greater Philadelphia area. It runs ASL classes, interpreter services, and community events such as a Deaf community day at the zoo and an ASL social night.
records.what_you_do: Take an ASL class, come to a community event such as a bingo night with ASL, or request an interpreter. The group also helps people get access to services, schools, and workplaces.

schedule.text: Classes and events on set dates. Listed upcoming events include a Deaf community day at the Philadelphia Zoo on Sept 20, 2026, a virtual Deaf sensitivity training on Oct 15, 2026, and a Bingo and ASL social on Nov 21, 2026. Class times are not on the page.

cost.text: Some events sell tickets through a link. Prices are not shown on the page we read.

access.notes: ASL interpreters are offered at the zoo event and through the site's interpreter request service. Captioning and wheelchair access are not stated.

first_step.how: Email info@dhcc.org or call 610-604-0452 to ask about the next ASL class or event, or join the mailing list on the site
first_step.basis: ASL classes and public events are listed with a published email and phone, though class times and prices are not on the page.

records.notes: No office address was on the pages read. The /contact/ and /about/ pages returned HTTP 404. Add a location once the office address is confirmed. A text line, 610-756-0330, is also published. The Bingo and ASL social is listed at 630 Fairview Road, but the city is not confirmed, so it is not recorded as a location.

records.name: Breakthrough: Deaf Advocacy ASL Club
records.summary: A twice-monthly ASL club at uCity Square in University City, run with Breakthrough: Deaf Advocacy. Members learn the basics of sign language and practice talking with Deaf community members.
records.what_you_do: Come to learn basic signs and practice conversation with Deaf community members.

schedule.text: Twice a month, according to the event listing. No session dates were shown on the listing read.

access.notes: The listing does not say whether an ASL interpreter or wheelchair access is provided. Ask the organizer before attending.

first_step.how: Use the Register section on the uCity Square listing to sign up for the next session
first_step.basis: The listing says the club covers the basics of ASL and has a sign-up step, but it does not say newcomers are welcome.

records.notes: The only source is a uCity Square event listing marked as a past event. No website for the organization was found (a guessed domain did not resolve), so the group's own schedule is unconfirmed. Two near-identical listings exist and may be duplicates. The listing names individual hosts, which are not recorded. If the next session cannot be confirmed, hold this record.

records.name: Penn In Hand
records.notes: A student group for University of Pennsylvania community members who use ASL. Its only public source is a February 2011 article, so it is not current. It is open only to the Penn community with no public sign-up. The contact is a student officer's personal university email, which is not recorded.

records.name: Hear Our Voices! Disability Conversations Group (WIHD)
records.notes: Run by the Westchester Institute for Human Development in Valhalla, New York. Its monthly group meets online by Zoom and is not a Philadelphia group. Recorded so it is not searched again.

notes: Searches: all 8 WebSearch calls used. Not run for lack of budget: a wider Philadelphia Deaf club search, the Keystone Chapter's own site, Breakthrough's own site, and a second pass on HLAA chapters. Fetches: about 37, including redirects and errors. Coverage: Philadelphia Adaptive Sports is not a separate organization in what was found, so the PCAS and PAR records cover that ground. No Deaf club with membership was found; the Deaf community entries are DHCC, the Breakthrough ASL club (listing only), and a monthly library gathering (blocked). Old, undated leads: a Virtual ASL Meetup Philly (Zoom, last seen 2021) and a Deaf and Hard of Hearing Meet Up in Manayunk (August 2022, passed); both are likely dormant and were not recorded. The HLAA national finder showed only 8 of 132 chapters on its first page, so other Philadelphia chapters may exist on later pages. The Arc of Philadelphia's older domain names (arcphila.org, thearcphila.org) did not resolve; arcphiladelphia.org is the working site. Penn In Hand is hidden as private. Out of scope: Hear Our Voices (New York). Dashes check: none used as punctuation.
